components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu hǎoduō péngyou.
example.english: He has a lot of friends.
example.fact: 好 here isn't its usual sense of "good" but works instead as an intensifier before 多 ("much, many"), similar to how colloquial English "a good many" uses "good" the same non-literal way — one of several set phrases (好久 "quite a while", 好几 "quite a few") where 好 means "quite, very" rather than "good."

examples.hanzi: 今天街上有好多人。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān jiē shang yǒu hǎo duō rén.
examples.english: There are so many people on the street today.

examples.hanzi: 吃了药以后,我感觉好多了。
examples.pinyin: Chī le yào yǐhòu, wǒ gǎnjué hǎo duō le.
examples.english: After taking the medicine, I feel much better.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — a picture of drops falling from the sky 一 through a cloud. As radical it marks weather, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 雾 fog.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ le.
example.english: It's raining outside.
example.fact: Chinese says 下雨 ("rain falls"), and the measure word is 场 or 阵: 一场大雨. 雨伞 is an umbrella, and the 雨 radical heads many weather characters like 雪, 雷 and 雾.

examples.hanzi: 雨下得很大，我们别出门了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ xià de hěn dà, wǒmen bié chūmén le.
examples.english: It's raining hard, so let's not go out.

examples.hanzi: 今天的雨把花都淋湿了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de yǔ bǎ huā dōu línshī le.
examples.english: Today's rain drenched the flowers.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 磅 is a pound, a heavy weight, as in 磅秤 scale.
旁 (páng) — close sound: 磅 bàng. 旁 also sounds out 膀 bǎng and 傍 bàng.

example.pinyin: Zhège bāo yǒu shí bàng zhòng.
example.english: This bag weighs ten pounds.
example.fact: 磅 is the weight pound (about 454 g), borrowed from English, while the currency pound uses a different character: 英镑. 磅秤 is a platform scale, and in 磅礴 (grand, majestic) it is read páng.

examples.hanzi: 他的体重是一百五十磅。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tǐzhòng shì yìbǎi wǔshí bàng.
examples.english: He weighs one hundred and fifty pounds.

examples.hanzi: 我们在磅秤上称了一下行李。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài bàngchèng shang chēng le yíxià xíngli.
examples.english: We weighed our luggage on the platform scale.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 警长带领警察调查这个案子。
example.pinyin: Jǐngzhǎng dàilǐng jǐngchá diàochá zhège ànzi.
example.english: The police chief led the officers in investigating this case.
example.fact: 长, here read zhǎng rather than the more common cháng ("long"), keeps its older sense of "chief, head, elder" — the same reading shows up in 校长 ("school principal"), 部长 ("department head"), and 家长 ("parent, head of household"), a whole family of "-长" leadership titles built the same way.

examples.hanzi: 警长对大家说:“大家要小心。”
examples.pinyin: Jǐngzhǎng duì dàjiā shuō: "Dàjiā yào xiǎoxīn."
examples.english: The sheriff told everyone, "Be careful."

examples.hanzi: 这位警长在小镇工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jǐngzhǎng zài xiǎozhèn gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
examples.english: This sheriff has worked in the small town for twenty years.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
亻 (person) — person radical; 佳 describes a fine person, then anything good, as in 最佳.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 佳 is jiā; 圭 also sounds out 挂 guà and 鞋 xié.

example.hanzi: 这是解决问题的最佳方法。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì jiějué wèntí de zuìjiā fāngfǎ.
example.english: This is the best way to solve the problem.
example.fact: 最 (built from 日 "sun" over 取 "to take, gather") pictures gathering everything under the sun — a natural superlative prefix for "-est, most" — combined here with 佳 ("fine, excellent," a quality more often applied to people or achievements) to give a somewhat more formal, written-register "best" than the everyday 最好.

examples.hanzi: 早上是学习的最佳时间。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang shì xuéxí de zuìjiā shíjiān.
examples.english: Morning is the best time to study.

examples.hanzi: 他被选为本届比赛的最佳球员。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi běn jiè bǐsài de zuìjiā qiúyuán.
examples.english: He was chosen as the best player of this tournament.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài xúnzhǎo shòuhàirén.
example.english: The police are searching for the victim.
example.fact: 受 (two hands, one giving 爫 and one receiving 又, passing something between them) contributes the sense of "to receive, to suffer," which 受害人 combines with 害 ("harm") and 人 ("person") into a fully transparent term: literally "a person who has received harm."

examples.hanzi: 受害人已经被送到医院了。
examples.pinyin: Shòuhàirén yǐjīng bèi sòng dào yīyuàn le.
examples.english: The victim has been taken to the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 这位受害人向警察说出了真相。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shòuhàirén xiàng jǐngchá shuō chū le zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: The victim told the police the truth.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 废 is a ruined building, then discarded.
发 (fā) — loose hint — 废 is fèi, close in sound to 发 fā.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.pinyin: Bié shuō fèihuà le, kuài diǎn zuòshì.
example.english: Stop talking nonsense, hurry up and get to work.
example.fact: 废 ("useless, abolished") plus 话 ("words, speech" — built from 讠 "speech" and 舌 "tongue") combine literally into "useless words"; 废话 also doubles as a sarcastic retort in speech ("废话!", roughly "No duh! Obviously!") when someone states something painfully obvious.

examples.hanzi: 我没有时间听你说废话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu shíjiān tīng nǐ shuō fèihuà.
examples.english: I don't have time to listen to your nonsense.

examples.hanzi: 他说的都是废话,一点儿用也没有。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì fèihuà, yìdiǎnr yòng yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: Everything he said was nonsense and of no use.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放, 收; 效 is to imitate or produce results.
交 (jiāo) — near sound — 效 is xiào; 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 较 jiào.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào de xiàoguǒ hěn hǎo.
example.english: This medicine is very effective.
example.fact: 果 ("fruit hanging from a tree," extended to "result") recurs across several common words for outcomes — 效果 ("effect"), 结果 ("result"), 如果 ("if", literally "as the result [would be]") — all built on the same underlying "fruit leads to result" metaphor, so recognizing 果 helps a learner guess the general sense of a whole family of words.

examples.hanzi: 这个方法效果怎么样?
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ xiàoguǒ zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How well does this method work?

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的特殊效果非常棒。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de tèshū xiàoguǒ fēicháng bàng.
examples.english: The special effects in this movie are great.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 医生正在处理他的伤口。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài chǔlǐ tā de shāngkǒu.
example.english: The doctor is treating his wound.
example.fact: 口 ("mouth," a simple picture of an open mouth) extends metaphorically in 伤口 to describe the "opening" a wound makes in the skin — the same "opening = mouth" metaphor appears in 门口 ("doorway," literally "gate mouth") and 河口 ("river mouth, estuary").

examples.hanzi: 他的手上有一个小伤口。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒu shang yǒu yí ge xiǎo shāngkǒu.
examples.english: There is a small cut on his hand.

examples.hanzi: 伤口不要碰水,会感染的。
examples.pinyin: Shāngkǒu bú yào pèng shuǐ, huì gǎnrǎn de.
examples.english: Don't get the wound wet, it can get infected.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 咯 is a sentence-final particle.
各 (gè) — close sound: 咯 gē/lo. 各 also sounds out 格 gé and 路 lù.

example.pinyin: Nà wǒmen zǒu lo.
example.english: Then let's go.
example.fact: 咯 is a casual sentence-final particle suggesting "so, that's how it is", softer than 了: 好咯, 对咯. The same character is also gē in 咯咯 (clucking, giggling).

examples.hanzi: 好咯，我们回家咯。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo lo, wǒmen huíjiā lo.
examples.english: Okay then, let's go home.

examples.hanzi: 你看，我说得没错咯。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn, wǒ shuōde méi cuò lo.
examples.english: See, I told you I was right.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 这个故事里的魔法非常神奇。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ de mófǎ fēicháng shénqí.
example.english: The magic in this story is truly wondrous.
example.fact: 法 (water 氵 flowing along a fixed course 去) originally meant "law, method" — the idea that even magic follows its own hidden rules; 魔法 pairs "demon, spirit" (魔, built on 鬼 "ghost") with that "method" sense, framing magic as a supernatural technique rather than pure chaos.

examples.hanzi: 哈利·波特是一个学魔法的男孩。
examples.pinyin: Hālì·Bōtè shì yí ge xué mófǎ de nánhái.
examples.english: Harry Potter is a boy who studies magic.

examples.hanzi: 她好像会魔法,什么都能变出来。
examples.pinyin: Tā hǎoxiàng huì mófǎ, shénme dōu néng biàn chūlái.
examples.english: She seems to know magic and can conjure up anything.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dúzì sànbù.
example.english: He likes to take walks by himself.
example.fact: 独自 doubles down on solitude by combining 独 ("alone, single" — its dog radical 犭 comes from an old association between a lone dog and solitary living) with 自 ("self," itself a pictograph of a nose, since ancient Chinese speakers pointed at their own nose to mean "me") — two independently "alone/self"-flavored characters reinforcing each other.

examples.hanzi: 我想独自去旅行一个星期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dúzì qù lǚxíng yí ge xīngqī.
examples.english: I want to travel alone for a week.

examples.hanzi: 她独自一人把孩子养大了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dúzì yì rén bǎ háizi yǎng dà le.
examples.english: She raised the child all by herself.

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.pinyin: Qǐng yòng xiànjīn zhīfù.
example.english: Please pay with cash.
example.fact: 现 contributes its "to appear, to be present" sense (from 见, "to see") to 现金, literally "money that is present, on hand right now" — distinguishing physical, immediately available cash from money that exists only as a number in an account or a future payment.

examples.hanzi: 我身上没带现金,可以刷卡吗?
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēn shang méi dài xiànjīn, kěyǐ shuā kǎ ma?
examples.english: I don't have any cash on me, can I pay by card?

examples.hanzi: 这家小店只收现金。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎo diàn zhǐ shōu xiànjīn.
examples.english: This little shop only takes cash.

components.note: 寸 (hand, also "inch") — a grasping hand seizing something; also in 对, 守, 寺.

example.pinyin: Tā duó dé le guànjūn.
example.english: He won the championship.
example.fact: 夺 means to take by force: 夺走 (to snatch), 夺取 (to seize). In sports news 夺冠 is shorthand for "to win the title". 夺目 means dazzling.

examples.hanzi: 他夺走了我手里的球。
examples.pinyin: Tā duózǒu le wǒ shǒu lǐ de qiú.
examples.english: He snatched the ball out of my hands.

examples.hanzi: 我们队夺得了第一名。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì duódé le dì-yī míng.
examples.english: Our team won first place.

meanings: to understand sth well and know how to use it

components.note: 手 (hand) — 手 as in 拿, 打, 拳; 掌 is the palm of the hand, then to control.
尚 (shàng) — near sound — 掌 is zhǎng; 尚 also sounds out 常 cháng, 堂 táng and 赏 shǎng.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 握 is to grasp, as in 握手 handshake.
屋 (wū) — near sound — 握 is wò; 屋 also sounds out 幄 wò.

example.hanzi: 这项技能他已经掌握了。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jìnéng tā yǐjīng zhǎngwò le.
example.english: He has already mastered this skill.
example.fact: 掌 names the palm of the hand, and 握 means "to grip tightly" — 掌握 literally "palm plus grip," a vivid image of physically holding something firmly in one's hand that extends metaphorically to mentally "grasping" a skill, a language, or a situation.

examples.hanzi: 他已经掌握了这门技术。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng zhǎngwò le zhè mén jìshù.
examples.english: He has already mastered this skill.

examples.hanzi: 我们要掌握好时间,别迟到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhǎngwò hǎo shíjiān, bié chídào.
examples.english: We need to manage our time well and not be late.

components.note: 来 (come, wheat) — traditional 麥 combined 來 (the old word for the wheat plant) with a foot 夂 — a grain brought in; 麦 is the wheat radical.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 请检查一下麦克有没有声音。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià màikè yǒu méiyǒu shēngyīn.
example.english: Please check whether the microphone has sound.
example.fact: 麦克 is a truncated, purely phonetic loanword — short for the fuller transliteration 麦克风 (màikèfēng, from English "microphone") — the same kind of clipping English does when it shortens "microphone" to "mic," just borrowed sound-by-sound into characters that otherwise mean "wheat" (麦) and "to overcome" (克).

examples.hanzi: 请把麦克递给他。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ màikè dì gěi tā.
examples.english: Please hand the microphone to him.

examples.hanzi: 主持人拿着麦克站在舞台中间。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔchírén ná zhe màikè zhàn zài wǔtái zhōngjiān.
examples.english: The host stands in the middle of the stage holding a microphone.

components.note: 儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.
童 (child) — as a sound unit, 童 also appears in 瞳 tóng and 撞 zhuàng; the character itself means child, as in 儿童.

example.hanzi: 这个公园有儿童游乐区。
example.pinyin: Zhège gōngyuán yǒu értóng yóulèqū.
example.english: This park has a children's play area.
example.fact: 儿童 is the neutral, written-register word for "child" — used in official contexts like 儿童节 ("Children's Day") — while 孩子 is the everyday spoken word for the same thing; 儿 by itself is a simple picture of a small child, drawn with an oversized head on a small body.

examples.hanzi: 儿童在公共场所要注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Értóng zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ yào zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: Children need to be careful in public places.

examples.hanzi: 六月一日是国际儿童节。
examples.pinyin: Liù yuè yī rì shì guójì Értóng Jié.
examples.english: June 1 is International Children's Day.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个女孩子在公园里跳舞。
example.pinyin: Nàge nǚháizi zài gōngyuán lǐ tiàowǔ.
example.english: That girl is dancing in the park.
example.fact: 女孩子 spells out "female child" in full by stacking 女 ("woman, female" — a pictograph of a kneeling, arms-crossed figure) directly onto 孩子 ("child"), where casual speech often just shortens it to 女孩 without the light final 子.

examples.hanzi: 这个女孩子今年才五岁,但很聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nǚháizi jīnnián cái wǔ suì, dàn hěn cōngmíng.
examples.english: This girl is only five this year, but she's very smart.

examples.hanzi: 她是个很爱笑的女孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge hěn ài xiào de nǚháizi.
examples.english: She is a girl who loves to laugh.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的军队非常强大。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jūnduì fēicháng qiángdà.
example.english: This country's military is very powerful.
example.fact: 强 (a bow 弓 strong enough to require great force to draw) pairs with 大 ("big," a person standing with arms and legs spread wide) into 强大, a word usually reserved for large-scale power — countries, armies, economies — rather than an individual's physical strength, which Chinese more often describes with 强壮.

examples.hanzi: 他的身体很强大,从来不生病。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ hěn qiángdà, cónglái bù shēngbìng.
examples.english: His body is strong and he never gets sick.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要一个强大的团队。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào yí ge qiángdà de tuánduì.
examples.english: We need a strong team.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 他们决定分开一段时间。
example.pinyin: Tāmen juédìng fēnkāi yí duàn shíjiān.
example.english: They decided to separate for a while.
example.fact: 分 (a knife 刀 cutting something already split 八) contributes "to divide," while 开 contributes "open, apart" (two hands 廾 lifting away a door's latch 一); 分开 combines "cutting apart" with "opening apart" into the general verb for separating two things, whether physical objects, a couple, or ideas.

examples.hanzi: 下班后,他们在路口分开了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān hòu, tāmen zài lùkǒu fēnkāi le.
examples.english: After work, they parted at the intersection.

examples.hanzi: 请把这些苹果分开放。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē píngguǒ fēnkāi fàng.
examples.english: Please put these apples separately.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain — rent was originally paid in grain, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
且 (qiě) — loose hint — 租 is zū; 且 also sounds out 组 zǔ and 祖 zǔ.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zū le yí tào gōngyù.
example.english: We rented an apartment.
example.fact: 租 works in both directions: 租房 (to rent a flat), 出租 (to rent out), 房租 (rent). 出租车 is a taxi, literally "for-rent car".

examples.hanzi: 这个房子的租金很贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángzi de zūjīn hěn guì.
examples.english: The rent for this house is very expensive.

examples.hanzi: 我想租一辆车去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zū yí liàng chē qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: I want to rent a car for a trip.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.

example.hanzi: 他是一位杰出的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi jiéchū de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: He is an outstanding scientist.
example.fact: 杰 is a bound form: 杰出 (outstanding), 杰作 (masterpiece), 豪杰 (hero). It is also a popular given name element, as in Jay Chou's Chinese name 周杰伦.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个杰出的作家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè jiéchū de zuòjiā.
examples.english: He is an outstanding writer.

examples.hanzi: 他的作品被称为杰作。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zuòpǐn bèi chēngwéi jiézuò.
examples.english: His work is called a masterpiece.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话, 请; 诺 is a spoken promise.
若 (ruò) — near sound — 诺 is nuò; 若 also sounds out 惹 rě.

example.hanzi: 他没有实现自己的承诺。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu shíxiàn zìjǐ de chéngnuò.
example.english: He didn't fulfill his own promise.
example.fact: 承 (multiple hands supporting something from below) contributes "to receive, to bear," while 诺 (speech 讠 plus the phonetic 若) names a spoken "yes, agreed" — 承诺 literally "to bear a spoken yes," framing a promise as a weight one agrees to carry, not just words spoken lightly.

examples.hanzi: 我对你的承诺不会改变。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì nǐ de chéngnuò bú huì gǎibiàn.
examples.english: My promise to you won't change.

examples.hanzi: 他承诺下个月一定还钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngnuò xià ge yuè yídìng huán qián.
examples.english: He promised to pay the money back next month.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 佬 is used for a man, as in 老佬 and 大佬 boss.
老 (lǎo) — same sound: 佬 lǎo. 老 means old and mature.

example.pinyin: Tā shì ge dàlǎo.
example.english: He is a big shot.
example.fact: 佬 comes from southern and Cantonese speech as a casual suffix for men, as in 港佬 or 广东佬. 大佬 originally meant boss or elder brother in Cantonese. In mainland slang 大佬 now means an expert, e.g. 技术大佬.

examples.hanzi: 他是我们村里的阔佬。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen cūn lǐ de kuòlǎo.
examples.english: He is the rich guy in our village.

examples.hanzi: 那个美国佬很爱说笑。
examples.pinyin: Nàge Měiguó lǎo hěn ài shuōxiào.
examples.english: That American guy loves joking around.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh radical (月 in 脸, 脑, 肚); 脖 is the neck.
孛 (bèi) — near sound — 脖 is bó; 勃 bó also shares it.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Chángjǐnglù de bózi hěn cháng.
example.english: A giraffe's neck is very long.
example.fact: 脖 carries the flesh radical ⺼ (a variant of 肉, "meat"), marking it as a body-part word, paired with the light noun suffix 子 also seen in 孩子 and 女孩子 elsewhere in this batch — the same suffix pattern that turns a bound root into an everyday, free-standing noun.

examples.hanzi: 天冷了,别忘了围上脖子。
examples.pinyin: Tiān lěng le, bié wàng le wéi shang bózi.
examples.english: It's cold now, don't forget to wrap up your neck.

examples.hanzi: 我睡觉姿势不对,脖子很疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shuìjiào zīshì bú duì, bózi hěn téng.
examples.english: I slept in a bad position and my neck hurts.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 检 first meant a wooden label or seal.
佥 (qiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn; also in 验 yàn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 险 xiǎn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: to look carefully inside.
祭 (jì) is a loose sound clue for chá; 祭 also sounds out 际 jì and 擦 cā.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.pinyin: Jiǎncháguān zài fǎtíng shàng fāyán.
example.english: The prosecutor spoke in court.
example.fact: 检 (originally a wooden tally used for checking records, from 木 "wood") and 察 (careful observation, under a roof 宀) both independently mean "to inspect, to examine" — 检察官 stacks two near-synonymous "to examine" characters onto 官 ("official") to name the official whose job is examining evidence and prosecuting a case.

examples.hanzi: 检察官正在认真地看这份材料。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎncháguān zhèngzài rènzhēn de kàn zhè fèn cáiliào.
examples.english: The prosecutor is reading this material carefully.

examples.hanzi: 他的梦想是做一名检察官。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì zuò yì míng jiǎncháguān.
examples.english: His dream is to become a prosecutor.

meanings: (of a movie, book, TV show etc) good

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This skirt looks very nice.
example.fact: 好看 literally combines "good" with "to look" (看, pictured as a hand 手 shading the eyes 目 to see into the distance) into "good to look at" — parallel to 好吃 ("good to eat, tasty") and 好听 ("good to listen to, pleasant-sounding"), a small family of "好 + sense-verb" adjectives covering different senses.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影真好看,我想再看一遍。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhēn hǎokàn, wǒ xiǎng zài kàn yí biàn.
examples.english: This movie is really good, I want to watch it again.

examples.hanzi: 她笑起来很好看。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiào qǐlái hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: She looks lovely when she smiles.

components.note: 门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话, 语; 谍 is a spy's report, as in 间谍.
枼 (yè) — near sound — 谍 is dié; 枼 also sounds out 蝶 dié and 碟 dié.

example.hanzi: 警方发现他是一名间谍。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng fāxiàn tā shì yì míng jiàndié.
example.english: The police discovered that he was a spy.
example.fact: 谍 rarely stands on its own and almost always pairs with words for covert information-gathering (间谍 "spy", 谍报 "espionage intelligence") — its 讠 (speech) component reflects that spying, in this character's core sense, is fundamentally about secretly reporting what one has learned.

examples.hanzi: 那个间谍后来被抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge jiàndié hòulái bèi zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: That spy was caught later.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸最喜欢看间谍电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zuì xǐhuan kàn jiàndié diànyǐng.
examples.english: My dad likes spy movies the most.

meanings: measure word for articles and essays

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — books were once bamboo strips, so ⺮ marks writing and chapters, as in 笔 pen, 简 simple; 篇 is an article.
扁 (biǎn) — close sound: 篇 piān. 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān and 遍 biàn.

example.hanzi: 我读了一篇有趣的文章。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dú le yì piān yǒuqù de wénzhāng.
example.english: I read an interesting article.
example.fact: 篇 is the measure word for complete written pieces: 一篇文章, 一篇作文, 一篇日记. The bamboo radical comes from the days when writing was done on strung bamboo slips.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章写得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng xiě de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This article is very well written.

examples.hanzi: 请把这几篇课文读一遍。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè jǐ piān kèwén dú yí biàn.
examples.english: Please read through these few texts.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.

example.hanzi: 这个玩具是给孩子的生日礼物。
example.pinyin: Zhège wánjù shì gěi háizi de shēngrì lǐwù.
example.english: This toy is a birthday present for the child.
example.fact: 玩 ("to play") is built from a truncated 玉 ("jade") plus 元 as a phonetic; its original sense was "to handle and admire a piece of jade" — a small hint of why 玩具 covers things handled purely for pleasure rather than utility.

examples.hanzi: 弟弟有很多玩具,房间里到处都是。
examples.pinyin: Dìdi yǒu hěn duō wánjù, fángjiān lǐ dàochù dōu shì.
examples.english: My little brother has many toys, and they're all over his room.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的玩具又好玩又便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de wánjù yòu hǎowán yòu piányi.
examples.english: The toys in this shop are fun and cheap.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 车上人很多,我们只能站着。
example.pinyin: Chē shàng rén hěn duō, wǒmen zhǐ néng zhànzhe.
example.english: There were a lot of people on the bus, so we could only stand.
example.fact: 车上 simply pairs 车 ("vehicle") with 上 ("on top of, aboard") — one of many Mandarin location phrases built from a place noun plus a directional word (里, 上, 下) rather than a preposition, the same pattern behind 手里 ("in hand") and 桌子上 ("on the table").

examples.hanzi: 你的手机是不是落在车上了?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī shì bu shì là zài chē shang le?
examples.english: Did you leave your phone in the car?

examples.hanzi: 车上很安静,大家都在睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Chē shang hěn ānjìng, dàjiā dōu zài shuìjiào.
examples.english: It's quiet in the car, and everyone is sleeping.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂用机器人生产汽车。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng yòng jīqìrén shēngchǎn qìchē.
example.english: This factory uses robots to produce cars.
example.fact: 机器人 is a modern coinage built from existing pieces — 机器 ("machine", itself already "device, mechanism") plus 人 ("person") — a transparent compound for "robot" rather than a phonetic loanword, unlike many other technology terms borrowed by sound from English.

examples.hanzi: 这个机器人会说话,还会跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jīqìrén huì shuōhuà, hái huì tiàowǔ.
examples.english: This robot can talk and even dance.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就想做一个机器人。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng zuò yí ge jīqìrén.
examples.english: He has wanted to make a robot since he was little.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.
足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.

example.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò ràng tā hěn mǎnzú.
example.english: This job makes him feel very satisfied.
example.fact: 满足 works as both a verb ("to satisfy a need," 满足需求) and an adjective describing a state ("to be satisfied," 很满足) with no change in form — another Mandarin verb doing double duty as a descriptive state, the same pattern as 工作 ("to work" / "a job").

examples.hanzi: 这点钱满足不了他的需要。
examples.pinyin: Zhè diǎn qián mǎnzú bù liǎo tā de xūyào.
examples.english: This little money can't meet his needs.

examples.hanzi: 她对现在的生活很满足。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì xiànzài de shēnghuó hěn mǎnzú.
examples.english: She is very content with her life now.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting on something: 放, 改, 政, 教; in 败 a blow breaking a cowry 贝 shell (valuable): ruin, defeat.
贝 (bèi) is a loose sound hint for bài.

example.hanzi: 我们队打败了对手,赢得了比赛。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì dǎbài le duìshǒu, yíngdé le bǐsài.
example.english: Our team defeated the opponent and won the match.
example.fact: 打败 is a resultative compound: 打 ("to hit") plus 败 ("to lose, be defeated") reads literally as "to hit into defeat" — the second character names the outcome of the first verb's action, which is also why the same word can flip to mean "to be defeated" depending on who's doing the hitting.

examples.hanzi: 他在决赛中打败了去年的冠军。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài juésài zhōng dǎbài le qùnián de guànjūn.
examples.english: He defeated last year's champion in the final.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能被困难打败。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng bèi kùnnan dǎbài.
examples.english: We must not be defeated by difficulties.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de yàoshi bú jiàn le.
example.english: My keys have disappeared. / I can't find my keys.
example.fact: 不 shifts from its usual bù to a 2nd tone, bú, when it falls right before another 4th-tone syllable like 见 — one of Mandarin's few genuine tone-sandhi rules, alongside the better-known one for 一.

examples.hanzi: 我找了半天,还是不见他的人影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo le bàntiān, háishi bú jiàn tā de rényǐng.
examples.english: I searched for ages and still couldn't see him.

examples.hanzi: 好久不见,你最近怎么样?
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, nǐ zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: Long time no see, how have you been?

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.pinyin: Wǒ quèxìn tā shuō de shì shíhuà.
example.english: I'm convinced that what he said is true.
example.fact: 确信 sits at the firmer, more certain end of Mandarin's "to believe" spectrum — stronger than the everyday 觉得 ("to feel/think") or 相信 ("to believe/trust"), 确信 implies the speaker has weighed the evidence and reached firm certainty, closer to English "convinced" than a plain "believe."

examples.hanzi: 我确信这个消息是真的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ quèxìn zhège xiāoxi shì zhēn de.
examples.english: I'm sure this news is true.

examples.hanzi: 你确信自己锁了门吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ quèxìn zìjǐ suǒ le mén ma?
examples.english: Are you sure you locked the door?

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 不管怎样,我都会支持你。
example.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, wǒ dōu huì zhīchí nǐ.
example.english: No matter what, I will support you.
example.fact: 不管怎样 belongs to a family of concessive phrases built on "不管 + question word" — 不管谁 ("no matter who"), 不管什么 ("no matter what"), 不管怎样 ("no matter how it turns out") — each naturally pairs with 都 later in the clause to mean "regardless, in every case."

examples.hanzi: 不管怎样,我们都要按时完成。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, wǒmen dōu yào ànshí wánchéng.
examples.english: Either way, we have to finish on time.

examples.hanzi: 不管怎样,谢谢你今天来看我。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, xièxie nǐ jīntiān lái kàn wǒ.
examples.english: Anyway, thank you for coming to see me today.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的传统节日。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de chuántǒng jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important traditional holiday.
example.fact: 传统 functions as both a noun ("a tradition") and an attributive adjective ("traditional," directly before a noun as in 传统节日) with no change in form at all — no suffix like English "-al" is needed to turn the noun into a modifier.

examples.hanzi: 我们家有每年一起包饺子的传统。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā yǒu měi nián yìqǐ bāo jiǎozi de chuántǒng.
examples.english: Our family has a tradition of making dumplings together every year.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢穿传统的中式衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chuān chuántǒng de Zhōngshì yīfu.
examples.english: She likes to wear traditional Chinese clothes.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).

example.pinyin: Tā zài yīyuàn de nèikē gōngzuò.
example.english: He works in the internal medicine department at the hospital.
example.fact: 科 is about categories: 内科 (internal medicine), 外科 (surgery), 科目 (subject), 科学 (science), 科长 (section chief). In biology, 科 is the taxonomic "family".

examples.hanzi: 我在大学学的是理科。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài dàxué xué de shì lǐkē.
examples.english: At university I studied science.

examples.hanzi: 这个科室的医生很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège kēshì de yīshēng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The doctors in this department are good.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 海, 河, 湖; 漫 is water overflowing, then spreading freely.
曼 (màn) — same sound — 漫 is màn; 曼 also sounds out 慢 màn.

example.hanzi: 巴黎是一座很浪漫的城市。
example.pinyin: Bālí shì yí zuò hěn làngmàn de chéngshì.
example.english: Paris is a very romantic city.
example.fact: 浪漫 is a phonetic borrowing of the Western word "romantic" — the characters 浪 ("wave") and 漫 ("to overflow, spread everywhere") were chosen mainly for sound and a loosely fitting sweeping, dreamy feel, even though neither character's original meaning has anything to do with romance itself.

examples.hanzi: 他给女朋友准备了一个浪漫的惊喜。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi nǚ péngyou zhǔnbèi le yí ge làngmàn de jīngxǐ.
examples.english: He prepared a romantic surprise for his girlfriend.

examples.hanzi: 海边的日落真浪漫。
examples.pinyin: Hǎibiān de rìluò zhēn làngmàn.
examples.english: The sunset by the sea is so romantic.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 哼 is humming or a snort.
亨 (hēng) — same sound: 哼 hēng. 亨 also sounds out 烹 pēng.

example.pinyin: Tā yìbiān zǒulù yìbiān hēng gē.
example.english: He hums a song as he walks.
example.fact: 哼 imitates a soft sound: 哼歌 (hum a tune), a snort of disdain (哼!) or a groan. In stories the "Heng and Ha" generals (哼哈二将) are guardian figures at temple gates.

examples.hanzi: 他哼着歌走进了房间。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēng zhe gē zǒu jìn le fángjiān.
examples.english: He hummed a song as he walked into the room.

examples.hanzi: 他哼了一声，没有回答。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēng le yì shēng, méiyǒu huídá.
examples.english: He gave a snort and didn't answer.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ niàn yíxià zhè jù huà.
example.english: Please read this sentence aloud.
example.fact: 念 means to read aloud (念课文) and to study (念大学, to attend university), both used colloquially. It also means to think of someone: 想念 (miss), 怀念 (cherish the memory of), 纪念 (to commemorate).

examples.hanzi: 我很想念我的家人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn wǒ de jiārén.
examples.english: I miss my family a lot.

examples.hanzi: 他在大学念书。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué niànshū.
examples.english: He studies at university.

components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.
黍 (millet) — the left part and radical, a grain plant. 黎 once meant 'black, many'; today it mostly appears in 巴黎 Paris and 黎明 dawn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí xiǎng qù Bālí lǚxíng.
example.english: I've always wanted to travel to Paris.
example.fact: 巴黎 is a pure phonetic transliteration of "Paris" — 巴 and 黎 were picked purely for sound, bā-lí approximating the French pronunciation, with neither character contributing any meaning, the same strategy behind other foreign names like 弗兰克 (also in this batch) for "Frank."

examples.hanzi: 巴黎的咖啡馆很有名。
examples.pinyin: Bālí de kāfēiguǎn hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: The cafés in Paris are very famous.

examples.hanzi: 他们去年夏天在巴黎结了婚。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen qùnián xiàtiān zài Bālí jié le hūn.
examples.english: They got married in Paris last summer.

meanings: variant of 重複|重复[chong2 fu4]

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 请不要重复同样的错误。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào chóngfù tóngyàng de cuòwù.
example.english: Please don't repeat the same mistake.
example.fact: 重 is a heteronym: read zhòng it means "heavy, important" (as in 重要), but read chóng it means "to repeat, layer upon layer" (as in 重复, 重新) — the same character splits into two unrelated readings depending on which sense is meant, a common trap for learners who default to the more frequent zhòng.

examples.hanzi: 请你把刚才的话重复一遍。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bǎ gāngcái de huà chóngfù yí biàn.
examples.english: Please repeat what you just said.

examples.hanzi: 这个文件里有很多重复的内容。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wénjiàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō chóngfù de nèiróng.
examples.english: There's a lot of repeated content in this file.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is the mouth, as in 吃, 喝, 叫; 和 is harmony and speaking together.
禾 (hé) — same sound — 和 is hé, like 禾.
平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.

example.pinyin: Quán shìjiè dōu xīwàng hépíng.
example.english: The whole world hopes for peace.
example.fact: 和 already carries a core sense of "harmony, accord" across many common words (和好 "to make up," 和谐 "harmonious"), and 平 contributes "level, even, calm" (as in 平静 "calm") — 和平 layers two near-synonymous "balanced, calm" characters into the abstract noun for the absence of conflict.

examples.hanzi: 我们都希望世界和平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xīwàng shìjiè hépíng.
examples.english: We all hope for world peace.

examples.hanzi: 两个国家用和平的方式解决了问题。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge guójiā yòng hépíng de fāngshì jiějué le wèntí.
examples.english: The two countries solved the problem in a peaceful way.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹, 歌; 欣 is joy showing.
斤 (jīn) — near sound — 欣 is xīn; 斤 also sounds out 新 xīn.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money or a gift, as in 财, 贵, 买; 赏 is a reward.
尚 (shàng) — same sound, different tone — 赏 is shǎng; 尚 also sounds out 掌 zhǎng and 常 cháng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng tā de cáihuá.
example.english: I really admire his talent.
example.fact: 赏 alone already means "to reward, to bestow" — its 贝 (valuables) component reflects an old sense of giving something valuable in recognition — and by extension came to mean "to appreciate the sight of" (赏花, "to admire flowers"); 欣赏 pairs it with 欣 ("delighted") to sharpen that appreciative sense.

examples.hanzi: 我很欣赏你做事认真的态度。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng nǐ zuòshì rènzhēn de tàidu.
examples.english: I really admire how seriously you approach your work.

examples.hanzi: 我们坐在窗边欣赏夜景。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò zài chuāng biān xīnshǎng yèjǐng.
examples.english: We sat by the window and enjoyed the night view.

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 他决定留下来照顾生病的母亲。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng liú xiàlái zhàogù shēngbìng de mǔqīn.
example.english: He decided to stay behind to take care of his sick mother.
example.fact: 留下来 chains three verb-like pieces into one phrase — 留 ("to remain, to leave behind"), 下 (a directional complement often marking something settling into place), and 来 (marking the action as oriented toward the speaker's here-and-now) — a common Mandarin strategy of building precise verb phrases from a core verb plus directional complements.

examples.hanzi: 你可以留下来吃晚饭吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ liú xiàlái chī wǎnfàn ma?
examples.english: Can you stay for dinner?

examples.hanzi: 大家都走了,只有他留下来打扫。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zǒu le, zhǐyǒu tā liú xiàlái dǎsǎo.
examples.english: Everyone left, and only he stayed behind to clean up.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.
example.english: The weather is very nice today.
example.fact: 气, a picture of rising wisps of vapor, is the shared root behind a whole family of words: 天气 ("weather"), 空气 ("air"), 生气 ("to get angry," literally "life-vapor rising"), and 气体 ("gas") all build on this one image of something invisible rising or flowing.

examples.hanzi: 明天天气怎么样?
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān tiānqì zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: What will the weather be like tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 天气太热了,我不想出门。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.english: It's too hot, and I don't want to go out.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — cord and silk: 红, 线, 给; 绑 is to bind with cord.
邦 (bāng) is a near sound match for bǎng.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xíngli bǎng jǐn.
example.english: Please tie the luggage down tightly.
example.fact: 绑 means to tie up firmly with a rope: 绑腿, 绑带. 绑架 is to kidnap. In apps 绑定 means to link an account, as in 绑定手机号 (link a phone number).

examples.hanzi: 他的手被绑住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒu bèi bǎngzhù le.
examples.english: His hands were tied up.

examples.hanzi: 请用绳子把箱子绑好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng shéngzi bǎ xiāngzi bǎnghǎo.
examples.english: Please tie up the box with a rope.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 老师把学生的名字一一念了出来。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ xuésheng de míngzi yīyī niàn le chūlái.
example.english: The teacher read out the students' names one by one.
example.fact: 一一, doubling the numeral "one," is one of the few reduplicated words in Mandarin built from a number rather than a verb or adjective — it works as an adverb meaning "individually, in sequence," placed right before the verb it modifies, distinct from the ordinary counting use of a lone 一.

examples.hanzi: 他把练习题一一做完了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ liànxí tí yīyī zuòwán le.
examples.english: He finished the exercises one by one.

examples.hanzi: 我会把你的问题一一回答。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì bǎ nǐ de wèntí yīyī huídá.
examples.english: I'll answer your questions one by one.
